issue_context.title: ACPI battery is not always "BAT0"
issue_context.body:
I just saw #23640 in the Git commits and noticed that it hardcodes `/sys/class/power_supply/BAT0` as the device path. But on a Dell Inspiron laptop here, there is no BAT0 device and the internal battery is `BAT1`:

```
$ ls /sys/class/power_supply/
ACAD
BAT1
```

Should probably be changed to look for `POWER_SUPPLY_TYPE=Battery` devices via sd-device.
comments: We are aware, support for multiple batteries will be added after BTP support. Those cases will simply work as they did before that PR until that happens (no regression).

yes. missed it. added
Ah, this comment explains my previous question. Could you move this comment to the relevant place in `get_total_suspend_interval()`?
Sure

Maybe, it is better to add an assertion for the timestamp?
```
assert(before_timestamp < after_timestamp);
```
`assert(ret)`
fixed
error check is missing
fixed
Is it not necessary to add a half hour??
Don't think so.... The suspend interval calculated has a margin of 30 minute to avoid losing state in case suspend interval is too low....

I asked that because in `get_total_suspend_interval()` you subtract 30min:
```
                suspend_interval = usec_sub_unsigned(battery_last_capacity * USEC_PER_HOUR / previous_discharge_rate, 30 * USEC_PER_MINUTE);

                total_suspend_interval += suspend_interval;
```
Why here 30min is subtracted??

E.g. if a laptop has a battery which is not charged enough, and `battery_last_capacity * USEC_PER_HOUR / previous_discharge_rate` is ~30min, then `get_total_suspend_interval()` may return timespan with only few seconds, and the caller use the timespan as is in `timespec_store()`... Is it expected?? That's super spurious for me.

That's not any different if the discharge rate was the same +30min, there's always a corner case where it sleeps for a very short amount of time. The important thing is that it doesn't go out of power and turns off while in suspend mode. That's what this 30 min buffer is for - to try and make that less likely to happen.
will take care of it.
Please insert an empty line between the system header and our custom header.

in our coding style, functions should either log about all errors, or about none (in which case it's up the caller to log or handle the error). This function logs in one error path via log_oom(), but not in the others.

usually functions that are "library-like" should not log on their own, and functions that are "main-program-like" should. But the lines are blurry and exceptions are OK. Hence, make up your mind what kind of function this should be, and then either add log calls on all error paths, or remove them from all and ensure you return an error properly.

here, i'd probably remove the log_oom() call up top, and just propagate `return r;`
